record.paper_title: Some Open Problems and Conjectures on Submanifolds of Finite Type: Revisited
record.original_question: For an isometric immersion x: M -> E^m with mean curvature vector H, call the immersion biharmonic when Delta^2 x = 0, equivalently Delta H = 0; minimal immersions are biharmonic. For complete submanifolds of Euclidean space, is every complete biharmonic submanifold minimal?

evidence.quote: Global Version of Chen’s biharmonic Conjecture: Every complete biharmonic submanifold of a Euclidean space is minimal.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $x: M \to \mathbb{E}^m$ be an isometric immersion of a Riemannian manifold $M$ into Euclidean $m$-space, and let $H$ denote its mean curvature vector field. Let $\Delta$ be the (negative-semidefinite, rough) Laplace-Beltrami operator of the induced metric, applied componentwise. The immersion is called biharmonic if $\Delta^2 x = 0$, which is equivalent to $\Delta H = 0$; any minimal immersion (i.e. one with $H \equiv 0$) is automatically biharmonic. Assume that $M$ is complete with respect to the induced metric. Prove or disprove: every complete biharmonic submanifold of $\mathbb{E}^m$ is minimal.
artifact.status_search_result: The global version of Chen's biharmonic conjecture remains open in general. It has been verified in several special cases: surfaces (Chen–Jiang, 1987), hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{E}^4$ (Hasanis–Vlachos, 1995), and for properly immersed complete biharmonic submanifolds (Akutagawa–Maeta and others). The case of hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{E}^5$ has been addressed in recent work, but the full conjecture for arbitrary complete biharmonic submanifolds in Euclidean space is not resolved.
